questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Task notifications and event groups”?
options: Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
A notification targets one task and is not a general-purpose data queue.
questions.answer: A notification targets one task and is not a general-purpose data queue.
questions.explanation:
A notification targets one task and is not a general-purpose data queue.
Why: A task notification sends a lightweight signal directly to one task and often uses less RAM than a separate queue for one receiver. `ulTaskNotifyTake` waits for that signal; event groups fit multiple consumers or sets of event bits. Ensure the task handle is valid and decide whether notifications accumulate or clear.
